target: A gente conhecia todos os vizinhos.
english: We used to know all the neighbors.
tip: Reflexive 'se' signals the subject acts on themselves: 'lavar-se' (wash oneself) vs. 'lavar' (wash something).

target: Ela limpou a casa inteira no sábado.
english: She cleaned the entire house on Saturday.
tip: Regular -ar past: limpar → limpou. 'A casa inteira' = the whole house. 'No sábado' = on Saturday.

target: Nós dissemos a verdade desde o começo.
english: We told the truth from the beginning.
tip: 'Dizer' past: nós dissemos. 'Desde o começo' = from the beginning.

target: Ele estudou a noite inteira para a prova.
english: He studied all night for the exam.
tip: Regular -ar past: estudar → estudou. 'A noite inteira' = the whole night. Time expression reinforces past.

target: A gente combinou de se encontrar no shopping.
english: We arranged to meet at the mall.
tip: Regular -ar past: combinar → combinou. 'Combinar de' = to agree to / to arrange. 'A gente combinou.'

target: Vocês cozinhavam ou comiam fora?
english: Did you use to cook or eat out?
tip: The impersonal 'se' makes generalizations without a specific subject: 'Come-se bem aqui' (One eats well here).

target: Eu soube da notícia pelo jornal.
english: I found out the news through the newspaper.
tip: 'Saber' in the past: soube, soube, soubemos, souberam. In the past, 'saber' often means 'to find out' rather than 'to know.'

target: Vocês deram uma olhada no projeto?
english: Did you take a look at the project?
tip: 'Dar' past: vocês deram. 'Dar uma olhada' = to take a look – a very common expression.

target: Nós voltamos de viagem ontem à noite.
english: We came back from the trip last night.
tip: Regular -ar past: voltar → voltamos (nós). The -amos ending is the same as present! Context tells which.

target: Vocês vieram de carro ou de ônibus?
english: Did you come by car or by bus?
tip: 'Vir' in the past: vim, veio, viemos, vieram. Don't confuse 'veio' (came) with 'viu' (saw).

target: Ele vinha de trem para a escola.
english: He used to come to school by train.
tip: 'Se' with transitive verbs can create passive meaning: 'Vendem-se casas' (Houses are sold / Houses for sale).

target: A gente viajou para Minas Gerais no feriado.
english: We traveled to Minas Gerais on the holiday.
tip: Regular -ar past: viajar → viajou. With 'a gente,' use third person singular: 'a gente viajou.'

target: A gente pôde descansar no final de semana.
english: We were able to rest on the weekend.
tip: 'Poder' past: a gente pôde. Note the circumflex: 'pôde' (past) vs. 'pode' (present).

target: A gente quis ir, mas não deu.
english: We wanted to go, but it didn't work out.
tip: 'Não deu' is extremely common Brazilian Portuguese for 'it didn't work out' or 'it wasn't possible.' Short for 'não deu certo.'

target: Eu sabia todas as músicas de cor.
english: I used to know all the songs by heart.
tip: Some verbs change meaning completely with 'se': 'lembrar' (remind) vs. 'lembrar-se' (remember); 'ir' (go) vs. 'ir-se' (leave).

target: Eu fui o primeiro a chegar na festa.
english: I was the first to arrive at the party.
tip: Here 'fui' comes from 'ser' (to be), not 'ir' (to go). 'Eu fui o primeiro' = I was the first. Context clarifies.

target: Eu não sabia nadar quando era pequeno.
english: I didn't know how to swim when I was young.
tip: Imperfeito of 'saber': sabia (eu). 'Saber' in imperfeito = used to know / didn't know (ongoing state).

target: Eu acordava cedo para pegar o ônibus.
english: I used to wake up early to catch the bus.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: acordava (eu). Habitual: 'I used to wake up early.' 'Para pegar' = to catch.

target: Ele ia à padaria buscar pão de manhã.
english: He used to go to the bakery to get bread in the morning.
tip: Some verbs are only used reflexively: 'arrepender-se' (to regret), 'queixar-se' (to complain). They have no non-reflexive form.

target: Fazia calor e o sol brilhava quando saímos de casa.
english: It was hot and the sun was shining when we left the house.
tip: Background description in imperfeito: 'fazia calor e o sol brilhava' sets the scene for 'saímos' (event).

target: Ele pôs a culpa em mim.
english: He put the blame on me.
tip: 'Pôr a culpa em' means to blame: 'pôs a culpa em mim' = he put the blame on me. Very common expression.

target: Vocês trouxeram protetor solar?
english: Did you bring sunscreen?
tip: Brazilian Portuguese: `você` is the default. Most Brazilians never say `tu`. `Você fala português?` is what you'll hear, with 3rd-person verbs.

target: Eu fiz tudo que pude.
english: I did everything I could.
tip: 'Fazer' past: eu fiz. 'Tudo que pude' = everything I could. 'Poder' past: eu pude.

target: Nós tivemos uma surpresa agradável.
english: We had a pleasant surprise.
tip: 'Ter' past: nós tivemos. 'Uma surpresa agradável' = a pleasant surprise.

target: Eu fiz uma besteira enorme.
english: I made a huge mistake.
tip: 'Fazer' past: eu fiz. 'Fazer besteira' = to do something stupid/make a blunder.

target: Eu pensava que sabia tudo.
english: I thought I knew everything.
tip: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'se' usually comes before the verb: 'Eu me levanto'. In European Portuguese, it follows: 'Levanto-me'.

target: Eu disse que não podia ir.
english: I said I couldn't go.
tip: 'Dizer' in the past: disse, disse, dissemos, disseram. The eu and ele/ela forms are the same: 'eu disse' = 'ele disse.'

target: Nós demos um presente para ela.
english: We gave her a gift.
tip: 'Dar' in the past: dei, deu, demos, deram. Short and irregular – very common forms to know.

target: Eu fiz as pazes com ela.
english: I made peace with her.
tip: 'Fazer as pazes' means to make up/reconcile after a fight. Always plural: 'as pazes,' never 'a paz' in this expression.

target: Vocês viram as cataratas do Iguaçu?
english: Did you see Iguaçu Falls?
tip: European Portuguese: `tu` is for close friends/family, `você` is slightly more distant. For real formality, drop the pronoun and use `o senhor` (m) / `a senhora` (f): `O senhor sabe...?`.

target: Vocês foram felizes nessa decisão.
english: You were happy with that decision.
tip: 'Ser/Ir' past: vocês foram. Here 'foram felizes' = were happy, so it's past of 'ser.'

target: Vocês disseram algo para ele?
english: Did you say anything to him?
tip: Plural: `vocês` is universal. Portugal also has `vós` but it's extinct in speech. Just use `vocês` and you're safe everywhere.

target: As férias duravam dois meses.
english: Vacations used to last two months.
tip: Imperfeito (`-ava/-ia` endings) paints background or habit: `quando era criança, jogava futebol` (as a kid, I used to play football). No clear endpoint.

target: Vocês viram aquele programa na TV?
english: Did you see that TV show?
tip: 'Ver' past: vocês viram. Don't confuse 'viram' (saw) with 'vieram' (came). 'Aquele programa' = that show.

target: Ela trouxe flores para a mãe.
english: She brought flowers for her mom.
tip: 'Trazer' past: ela trouxe. 'Trouxe flores para a mãe' = brought flowers for (her) mom.

target: Ela veio de avião do Recife.
english: She came by plane from Recife.
tip: 'Vir' (to come) → 'veio' (he/she came). Don't confuse with 'viu' from 'ver' (to see).

target: Eu trouxe um souvenir para você.
english: I brought a souvenir for you.
tip: 'Trazer' → 'trouxe.' The stem changes completely: traz- → troux-.

target: Ele disse que estava cansado demais.
english: He said he was too tired.
tip: 'Estava' is the imperfect of 'estar' – describes ongoing states or conditions in the past.

target: Ela disse que vai pensar no assunto.
english: She said she'll think about it.
tip: 'Dizer' past: ela disse. 'Disse que vai' – the reported speech keeps the original tense in casual Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Eu fiz uma promessa para mim mesmo.
english: I made a promise to myself.
tip: Portuguese irregular preterites share patterns with Spanish – learning one helps with the other.

target: A cidade era menor e mais calma.
english: The city was smaller and calmer.
tip: Reflexive verbs in Portuguese often express emotional states: 'sentir-se' (feel), 'zangar-se' (get angry), 'preocupar-se' (worry).

target: Eu vi um acidente na estrada.
english: I saw an accident on the road.
tip: 'Ver' in the past: vi, viu, vimos, viram. Very short forms – don't confuse 'vi' (I saw) with 'vim' (I came).

target: Ele pôs as chaves na mesa.
english: He put the keys on the table.
tip: 'Pôr' in the past: pus, pôs, pusemos, puseram. In casual speech, many Brazilians say 'coloquei' instead of 'pus.'

target: Eu tive que trabalhar no feriado.
english: I had to work on the holiday.
tip: 'Ter' past: eu tive. 'Tive que' = I had to (obligation). 'No feriado' = on the holiday.

target: Ele veio me visitar de surpresa.
english: He came to visit me by surprise.
tip: 'Vir' past: ele veio. 'Veio me visitar' = came to visit me. 'De surpresa' = as a surprise.

target: O restaurante estava cheio quando chegamos.
english: The restaurant was full when we arrived.
tip: 'Estava cheio' (imperfeito, description) + 'chegamos' (perfeito, event). Scene + arrival pattern.

target: A gente teve sorte de encontrar lugar.
english: We were lucky to find a spot.
tip: 'Ter' past: a gente teve. 'Ter sorte de' = to be lucky to. Remember 'a gente' = singular.

target: Eu trouxe o documento que você pediu.
english: I brought the document you asked for.
tip: 'Trazer' past: eu trouxe. Note the stem change: traz- → troux-. 'Que você pediu' = that you asked for.

target: Eu disse que concordava com a proposta.
english: I said I agreed with the proposal.
tip: Regular -ar verbs in the imperfect: -ava, -ava, -ávamos, -avam – note the accent on 'ávamos'.

target: Estou guardando dinheiro para comprar uma casa.
english: I'm saving money to buy a house.
tip: Endings: -ar → -ando, -er → -endo, -ir → -indo. `Comendo`, `bebendo`, `dormindo`. Always paired with `estar`.

target: Nós demos a volta na cidade de bicicleta.
english: We went around the city by bike.
tip: 'Dar' past: nós demos. 'Dar a volta' = to go around. 'De bicicleta' = by bicycle.

target: Nós almoçávamos juntos todo dia.
english: We used to have lunch together every day.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: almoçávamos (nós). The -ávamos ending is always stressed on the 'á.'

target: Ela morava perto da praia antes.
english: She used to live near the beach before.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: morava (ela). Regular: morar → morava. Used for habitual past or background states.

target: Ela tomava sorvete depois da escola.
english: She used to eat ice cream after school.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: tomava (ela). Habitual past: 'she used to have ice cream.' 'Sorvete' = ice cream.

target: Eu soube que ele vai se mudar.
english: I found out that he's going to move.
tip: 'Saber' past: eu soube. 'Soube que' = I found out that. Past of 'saber' implies learning new info.

target: Eu soube que ela passou no concurso.
english: I heard she passed the civil service exam.
tip: 'Concurso' in Brazil refers to competitive civil service exams. Passing one is a huge achievement and guarantees a stable government job.

target: Nós comíamos pamonha na época da colheita.
english: We used to eat pamonha during harvest time.
tip: Pamonha is a traditional Brazilian snack made from fresh corn wrapped in corn husks. Very popular in the countryside and during festas juninas.

target: Nós trocamos a TV por uma maior.
english: We exchanged the TV for a bigger one.
tip: 'Por' for exchange/substitution: 'trocar A por B' = to exchange A for B.

target: Ela deu uma festa surpresa para o marido.
english: She threw a surprise party for her husband.
tip: 'Dar' past: ela deu. 'Dar uma festa' = to throw a party. 'Festa surpresa' = surprise party.

target: Eu queria ser astronauta quando era criança.
english: I wanted to be an astronaut as a kid.
tip: Imperfeito of -er: queria (eu). 'Querer' imperfeito is regular: queria. 'Quando era criança' sets the past scene.
